summary: Introductory discovery focused on integration patterns: using Redwood hosted vs Dedicated vs Private behind an edge gateway/proxy, SDK support for LangChain/LlamaIndex, rate limiting and quotas at the gateway level, and observability hooks. Customer is evaluating production footprint for an app that does long-context summarization and retrieval augmented generation (RAG).
topics: Rate limits / quotas and per-route policies
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-21 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~38 min | Recording: Fireflies auto
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Sanjay Reddy (Orion CTO), Lena Park (Orion Lead ML Eng), Marco Ruiz (Orion Platform)

00:00 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time. Quick intro, I'm Maya, AE on the account, and with me is Daniel our solution engineer.
00:18 - Daniel Ortiz: Hi all, hi, thank you. Quick note, I'll jump into the architecture questions and demo some integration patterns after we hear what you folks are running.
00:33 - Sanjay Reddy: Cool. Thanks. Short background, Orion's building a summarization pipeline over long-doc ingest, RAG steps, we expect ~50 to 200 qps during peak, with sporadic big batch jobs. We're exploring Redwood for inference because of the low-latency needs and the SLOs.
00:50 - Lena Park: Yeah and we use LangChain for orchestration and LlamaIndex on the retrieval side, so we care about token continuity, KV cache, and also a gateway that does auth and rate-limiting.
01:05 - Maya Chen: Perfect, that matches a lot we've seen. Quick qualifier: are you leaning hosted first or more private/dedicated from day one?
01:18 - Sanjay Reddy: We're leaning hosted to move fast but need the option to go private for compliance — some customers will demand data residency and VPC.
01:30 - Daniel Ortiz: Makes sense. Redwood's patterns: hosted API for fast onboarding, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC or on-prem) when you need network isolation and KMS controls. For the gateway piece, are you running Envoy today?
01:45 - Marco Ruiz: We run Envoy as our edge, with Kong on some older services. We need per-route rate-limits: different tiers for free vs paid customers, plus a global token budget.
02:05 - Daniel Ortiz: Ok, good. We typically see two approaches: 1) Put Redwood behind your gateway as a downstream service — you proxy requests through and handle auth/rate-limits at the gateway; or 2) use a lightweight token exchange at the gateway and call Redwood directly from service nodes with client SDKs. Both work; tradeoffs are around observability and routing.
02:23 - Lena Park: Can you run through what SDKs look like for LangChain and LlamaIndex specifically? Any gotchas?
02:35 - Daniel Ortiz: Yeah. Our Python SDK supports direct LangChain connectors — we've got an example repo. For LlamaIndex, it's typically a custom llm wrapper; the main gotchas are streaming responses and incremental token handling. Also prefix KV cache invalidation can be tricky with long contexts.
02:53 - Lena Park: By prefix KV you mean the token-level cache for decoder state, right? Sometimes LamaIndex (sic) will reconstruct prompts and break cache hits.
03:05 - Daniel Ortiz: Exactly. If you're using heavy retrieval that's modifying prompts, you might lose some continuous kv-cache benefits. We recommend a batching window and explicit cache keys for RAG flows.
03:18 - Sanjay Reddy: Rate limits — do you expose per-key quotas we can read? We want to enforce at the gateway but also show per-user usage in our dashboards.
03:30 - Maya Chen: Redwood provides token-level usage metrics via the Console and API, and per-key quotas can be enforced server-side in Hosted. For Dedicated and Private, you can push metrics into your observability stack and enforce quotas at the gateway. We also expose per-route cost estimates.
03:50 - Marco Ruiz: How do we handle retries and idempotency? Our gateway does retries on 502/504. If a generation retries, we need to avoid double-billing or duplicate outputs.
04:05 - Daniel Ortiz: Good point. We give you an idempotency token you can pass to create requests; on our side we map token to a request-result mapping for a TTL. For streaming or long-running jobs, we recommend an initial handshake call to reserve a job id then stream chunks referencing that id. Retries then are safe.
04:25 - Lena Park: Observability hooks — we need distributed traces that correlate our request id with Redwood tokens. Is there a tracing header we propagate?
04:36 - Daniel Ortiz: We support standard tracing headers (W3C traceparent) and also allow you to pass in a request_id in metadata. That metadata shows up in the Console logs and in exported traces. We also surface per-token timing breakdowns — kernel time, network, kv cache hits — in the Console.
04:58 - Sanjay Reddy: Nice. For Private deployments, what's the usual network topology? We need VPC peering and a customer-managed KMS.
05:12 - Maya Chen: For Private we run a control plane that can optionally be hosted; the compute sits in your VPC or on-prem. KMS integration (Bring Your Own KMS/HSM) is supported, and audit logs can stream to your SIEM. We'll share the private deployment checklist.
05:28 - Marco Ruiz: Do you support on-prem bare metal? Some workloads must not leave our datacenter.
05:35 - Daniel Ortiz: Yes, we have an on-prem package for air-gapped scenarios; it requires extra setup — network, storage for weights, and we've got a special security hardening playbook.
05:48 - Sanjay Reddy: Cost controls — can we do per-tenant cost caps or soft limits?
05:56 - Maya Chen: On Hosted we have quotas and hard limits on tokens per-api-key. Dedicated gives you predictable unit economics since you reserve capacity. Private is you run the infra so cost controls are your responsibility, though our Console supports accounting and chargeback reports.
06:14 - Marco Ruiz: Gateway pattern question: we want to avoid spiky bursts swamping Redwood — can you do burst handling?
06:23 - Daniel Ortiz: Yes, we support burst capacity on Dedicated — you can config a shaped burst window. Also prefix caching and local batching minimize upstream bursts. On the gateway, you can implement a token bucket per-user then smooth requests into Redwood at the edge.
06:40 - Lena Park: SDK latency — what's typical p99 for a 1k token generation on Hosted?
06:48 - Daniel Ortiz: It depends on model and sequence length but we've seen p99 numbers in the 700–1200ms range for optimized Llama-ish models on hosted with streaming off. For longer contexts it's higher; we'll run a benchmark for your 2k case.
07:05 - Sanjay Reddy: Is multi-model routing supported? We might route cheaper quantized versions for lower tiers.
07:12 - Maya Chen: Absolutely. Smart routing rules can pick model variant by policy — cost-first for free tiers, high-quality for enterprise. Automatic fallback if a variant is unavailable.
07:25 - Marco Ruiz: About LlamaIndex integration specifically — any shims for callback handlers so the index can stream tokens as they arrive?
07:35 - Daniel Ortiz: We have a streaming callback interface; the LangChain and LlamaIndex wrappers include hooks. Caveat: make sure your callback handler is idempotent, especially with retries.
07:50 - Lena Park: How do you expose internal metrics? We ingest into Datadog and Prometheus.
07:58 - Daniel Ortiz: For Hosted we provide exports and webhooks; for Dedicated/Private you can pull Prometheus metrics and configure exporters; we also have a Datadog integration to push traces and metrics.
08:14 - Sanjay Reddy: Security: we must have SAML SSO for our internal console access and RBAC.
08:23 - Maya Chen: Supported. SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC are all supported for enterprise tiers. We'll send the SCIM SSO docs.
08:33 - Marco Ruiz: When you say per-route cost estimates, is that live? We want to show customers estimated charge before sending long requests.
08:42 - Daniel Ortiz: We can return cost estimates synchronously given tokens and model selection; that's what some customers do to show a preview on the UI. For streamed responses, we also give incremental estimates.
08:58 - Sanjay Reddy: Anything to watch for with LangChain orchestration? We do chains with multiple LLM calls.
09:08 - Daniel Ortiz: For multi-call chains, trace and the request_id propagation is key. Also prefer batching where you can — aggregate multiple short prompts when latency allows. And watch for prompt growth — chain steps concatenating can blow up token count and cost.
09:28 - Lena Park: On the SDK, do you provide retry/backoff defaults? We have a circuit breaker layer but want library best-practices.
transcript_continued:
09:38 - Daniel Ortiz: SDKs have sane retry/backoff defaults and exponential backoff, plus status codes to differentiate retryable errors. We also provide guidance for circuit breakers.
10:02 - Sanjay Reddy: We plan to front Redwood with our gateway so we can do canary releases per customer. Any tips?
10:12 - Maya Chen: Canarying with routing rules is common — use per-customer routing keys and have fallback to a stable model. Use the Console to set rollout percentages and monitor quality metrics.
10:25 - Marco Ruiz: How do you measure quality regressions? We need automated alerts if a model rollout degrades our prompts.
10:34 - Daniel Ortiz: Redwood Optimize ties a prompt set to evals and can trigger regression alerts. You define your held-out prompts, we run nightly evals and can route traffic back if thresholds fail.
10:47 - Lena Park: Any known integration issues with LlamaIndex embeddings? We use custom embedder currently.
10:56 - Daniel Ortiz: No major blockers — embeddings are agnostic as long as you normalize vectors. Watch for normalization mismatches between offline and runtime.
11:10 - Sanjay Reddy: Regarding quotas in the gateway, we were thinking per-minute token buckets and a monthly cap. Can we map a user to an api-key with different quotas?
11:24 - Maya Chen: Yes — a common architecture: API gateway maps user to account key and applies per-tier rate limit. Redwood's Hosted supports per-key quotas; Dedicated/Private you enforce at gateway and sync usage metrics for billing.
11:38 - Marco Ruiz: How do you handle partial responses if a stream is terminated early? We need deterministic behavior for consumers.
11:48 - Daniel Ortiz: Streams can be closed with a terminal code and we provide partial output and a truncated flag. The SDK can rehydrate with the same idempotency key to continue if the backend still has cached state.
12:05 - Lena Park: Anything about model quantization for Dedicated? We may want 4-bit models for cost savings.
12:13 - Daniel Ortiz: We support quantized variants; Dedicated pools can be provisioned with quantized kernels for throughput. We can recommend quantization profiles based on your evals.
12:28 - Sanjay Reddy: Can you run a quick sketch of the recommended architecture for our use case?
12:36 - Daniel Ortiz: Sure — quick sketch: Your edge (Envoy) does auth + per-tenant rate-limit, then either proxy to Redwood hosted (fast path) or route to an internal service that calls Redwood Dedicated/Private via SDK for low-latency needs. Add a local prefix cache for repeated prompts, and a background batcher for less-latency-sensitive jobs. Monitor with Datadog traces and use request_id propagation.
13:05 - Marco Ruiz: For the proxy approach, is TLS mutual auth an option? We want mTLS to Redwood endpoints from our gateways.
:13:18 - Maya Chen: mTLS is supported for Private connections. For Hosted we support TLS with client certs in some enterprise arrangements — will confirm in the checklist.
13:30 - Sanjay Reddy: About billing and logs — can we get detailed per-call logs for audit?
13:39 - Maya Chen: Yes, audit logs can include payload metadata, tokens used, timestamps. For privacy we redact user PII upon request.
13:52 - Lena Park: Any pitfalls with LlamaIndex streaming callbacks around incremental indexing?
14:00 - Daniel Ortiz: If your index mutates mid-stream, ensure you snapshot the index state or use a write-ahead log pattern to avoid inconsistencies; otherwise you can get non-deterministic reruns on retries.
14:15 - Sanjay Reddy: What about upgrade windows for Dedicated? We need to schedule model and runtime upgrades without impacting SLAs.
14:25 - Maya Chen: We support canary deploys with automated rollback if latency or error rates spike. For Dedicated we coordinate maintenance windows and provide pre-upgrade benchmarks.
14:40 - Marco Ruiz: Are SDKs open-source? We want to audit the client.
14:47 - Daniel Ortiz: Yes, our SDKs are OSS on GitHub. We'll link the repo.
14:53 - Maya Chen: Quick recap, we heard: you want hosted to start, with an option to move to Dedicated/Private; gateway pattern is Envoy with per-route quotas; important integration points are LangChain/LlamaIndex SDKs and streaming callbacks; must-have security is SSO, VPC, KMS. Next steps we discussed are benchmarks, docs, and a follow-up gateway deep-dive.
15:13 - Sanjay Reddy: Sounds right. One more, do you have a sample rate-limit config for Envoy?
15:20 - Daniel Ortiz: We do, we'll share a sample with token-bucket examples and a smoothing window.
15:29 - Marco Ruiz: I'll drop our current envoy config into the shared folder.
15:34 - Lena Park: Also please include the skeleton for the LangChain wrapper — that would accelerate our prototype.
15:41 - Maya Chen: Absolutely, we'll drop the LangChain/LlamaIndex examples and the Private deployment checklist.
15:48 - Sanjay Reddy: Great, thanks — let's reconvene after the benchmarks.
15:52 - Maya Chen: Thanks all. End.
